lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: # Deliver Host Control in three slices, with the companion as the command listener

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: **Host Control** lets a **Deck App** ask a nearby Mac or Windows computer to run a typed command (launch an app, send a media key). Draft PR #16 designed and built it as one 50-file change: SDK contract, companion CLI, a `sceHttp` client on the Vita, vendored picohttpparser, a rewritten upload server, and an always-on LAN listener that changed the **Runtime Upload** lifecycle. It was closed because it could not be reviewed or rebased. This ADR keeps the parts of that design that held up and drops the rest.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: ## Delivery

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: Host Control lands as three PRs. Each one builds, tests, and merges on its own. (b) and (c) depend only on (a), so they can run in parallel.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: 1. **Wire contract and SDK client.** `protocolVersion`, a typed command registry, machine error codes, and the JSON result shape **Runtime Upload POST** already uses (`ok: true` plus fields, or `ok: false` with `code` and `message`). The only commands are `host.capabilities` and `host.echo`. It ships as an additive subpath export of `@vitadeck/sdk`, so it is part of the author contract from day one. The client takes its base URL and transport as arguments, so its tests need neither a Vita nor a companion.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: 2. **Host Companion CLI.** A TypeScript workspace package, not published to npm in v1. It serves commands and performs **Host Control Link**. Its tests run against a TypeScript stand-in for the Vita link endpoint.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: 3. **Native link and Shell connection screen.** The Vita link endpoint, the persisted callback URL, a native getter that the SDK client reads, and a **VitaDeck Shell** screen showing the Vita address, the linked computer, and a way to forget the link. This slice needs the `full` agent-check tier.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: ## Topology

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: **Recommended default, pending Máté's confirmation:** link once, then the Vita calls the companion. This is option C in #16's topology comparison, and it is what the branch shipped.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: The user reads an address on the Vita's Shell connection screen and gives it to the **Host Companion**. The companion sends one link request with its protocol version, its name, and the callback URL where it accepts commands. VitaDeck stores that URL and sends each later command to it as an HTTP POST. The companion is the long-lived listener. The Vita listens only while the Shell connection screen is open, and stops when a link succeeds or the user cancels. That matches the **Runtime Upload Listener** lifecycle, and the link endpoint stays separate from that listener rather than becoming #16's always-on server shared with upload.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: This is the only option that meets the pairing goal ("type the Vita's address on the computer") without running a session server on the Vita. Steady-state commands need no new native code: Deck Apps already have `fetch()` on libcurl, with completions on a worker thread, on both targets. That makes #16's 650-line `sceHttp` client unnecessary. The Vita is exposed on the LAN only briefly, and only when the user asks for it. A new TCP connection per command costs a few milliseconds on a home LAN, which is fine for button presses.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: Accepted costs:

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: - The companion needs an inbound firewall rule.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: - A stale callback URL (a DHCP change, or the companion restarting on another port) breaks commands until the user links again.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: - The computer cannot push events to the Vita.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: **Alternative (option B):** the companion dials in and holds a persistent WebSocket or long-poll session with the Vita. That gives lower per-command latency and lets the computer push to the Vita. The cost is a WebSocket or long-poll server, a command queue, and reconnect logic in Vita C, which is the riskiest native work in this initiative and all of it has to exist before the first command works.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: ## HTTP parsing

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: **Recommendation:** extract and extend the upload server's parsing. Do not vendor picohttpparser now.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: Under the recommended topology, the Vita parses exactly one new kind of request: a small JSON link POST with `Content-Length`, answered with `Connection: close`. `src/upload/http_server.c` already reads that shape. Slice (c) moves its request-line, header, and body reading into a module that both listeners call, and fixes its one real defect along the way: it matches header names case-sensitively. Browsers and curl send `Content-Length`, but Node's built-in `fetch` sends `content-length`, so the companion's link request would get a 400 today. #16's spike showed that picohttpparser compiles for the Vita without patches. It did not show that the Vita needs it. Two parsers in the tree would mean two behaviours for the same bytes. picohttpparser remains the fallback if the Vita ever needs keep-alive, pipelining, or chunked bodies, which would happen if option B is chosen.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: ## Deferred

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: - **Linux companion.** macOS and Windows come first. Nothing in the contract depends on the platform.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: - **Command catalogue.** Every command beyond `host.capabilities` and `host.echo` is its own later PR, with per-platform implementations.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: - **Internet or account pairing.** Host Control is LAN only.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: - **Credentials.** v1 trusts the LAN, like the initial **Runtime Upload**. The companion therefore accepts commands from any LAN peer. That is harmless for `echo`, but not for launching apps, so a credential decision must come before the first command that acts on the computer.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: **Host Control Link** is not **Upload Pairing**. A link exchanges an address and authorizes nothing. **Upload Pairing** is a future, ephemeral credential scoped to the **Runtime Upload Listener**. When Host Control needs a credential, the likely shape is the same idea: a short-lived code shown on the Vita and entered on the companion. At that point, either widen **Upload Pairing** to cover both listeners or add a sibling term. Decide then; do not overload the term now. Internet pairing is neither.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: **Considered options:** rebase #16 (rejected: four months stale, and it couldn't be reviewed as one change). Topology A, where the user types the computer's address on the Vita (rejected: wrong pairing direction, and it needs a Shell text editor). Topology B (see the alternative above). One always-on LAN listener for upload and Host Control (rejected: it changes the Runtime Upload lifecycle for no Host Control need). A second HTTP client on `sceHttp` (rejected: `fetch()` already covers it).

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: docs(adr): host control sliced delivery and topology (#70)
lines.text: **Consequences:** slices may lift code from #16 (the SDK registry, the companion gateway) but not its shared listener, `sceHttp` client, or picohttpparser. The Runtime Upload lifecycle and its glossary entries stay as they are. If option B is chosen instead, rewrite this ADR and the HTTP parsing recommendation together.
